title: ZAKA volunteers from Israel go out to rescue and save lives in disasters, from Thailand to Venezuela

trailer.text: ZAKA is a rescue and volunteer organization founded by Yehuda Meshi-Zahav in 1995, according to the organization's website.
According to the article, at the time of writing ZAKA had 48 international forces, and it still sent volunteers from Israel around the world.

paragraphs.text: One of the haredi yeshiva students who ran to the scene of the attack on Bus 405 to give first aid was Yehuda Meshi Zahav, who went on to found ZAKA.
Meshi-Zahav came with yeshiva students to give first aid to the injured.
Meshi-Zahav went on to found ZAKA.
According to the organization's website, he founded it in 1995.
Date of the attack on bus 405, according to the article in eJewishPhilanthropy: July 6, 1989
On July 6, 1989, a 25-year-old terrorist from Islamic Jihad attacked the driver of Egged bus 405, near Neve Ilan on the outskirts of Jerusalem.
In the attack, 16 people were killed, among them two Canadians and an American, and 27 were injured.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Jewish law demands utmost respect for the dead, including a prompt burial and burial of every part of the body.
According to the same newspaper, collecting remains after a terrorist attack is not a task that the police and Magen David Adom paramedics are trained for.
Yeshiva students led by their rabbi rushed to help collect the remains, together with Arab residents from Ein Rafa and Ein Nakuba.
According to ynet, once the wounded had been evacuated, dozens of volunteers went down into the wadi and attended to the dead, the bloodstains and the remains that require burial.

stations.title: From the wadi to an organization

paragraphs.text: According to the organization's website, for thirty years Meshi-Zahav was a member of the Eda Haredit in Mea Shearim and took part in demonstrations against the Zionist establishment.
According to the Forward, until a few years before ZAKA was founded he was the public face of the Eda Haredit.
According to an article in eJewishPhilanthropy, Meshi-Zahav realized that in a disaster the police barricade the scene and only allow “official” people access, and so his team became professional.
According to The Jerusalem Post, he set up a formal nonprofit organization, which was recognized by the government in 1995.
According to the organization's website, ZAKA's unique purpose is to ensure a full Jewish burial for victims of unnatural death, whether by accident, terror attack or natural disaster.
According to ynet, the mission is summed up in one sentence: to save those who can be saved and to honor those who can now only be honored.

stations.title: At home: volunteers in every district

paragraphs.text: According to a letter by ZAKA founder and chairman Yehuda Meshi Zahav on the organization's website, ZAKA has over 3,000 volunteers deployed throughout Israel, on call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Later, the organization also began receiving requests to help locate a person who was lost in the desert or had gone missing on a camping trip.
According to a 2010 report, ZAKA has a minorities unit of Bedouin, Muslim and Druze volunteers, established to serve Israel's non-Jewish communities.
According to the organization's chairman, ZAKA trains with the IDF Home Front Command and works with it when the home front becomes the front line.

stations.title: At the scene, to the last drop

paragraphs.text: According to the Times of Israel, ZAKA volunteers are usually at the scenes of terror attacks and deadly road accidents, collecting body remains and blood for Jewish burial according to Jewish law.
According to the organization's website, they are always the last to leave such a scene, after clearing away the blood and human remains.
According to ZAKA's director-general in the eJewishPhilanthropy article, volunteers who were already at the scenes, and could not watch without helping, began training as emergency responders.
According to eJewishPhilanthropy, in 2001 the Versailles wedding hall in Jerusalem collapsed in the middle of a wedding; 23 people fell to their deaths and 380 were injured.
According to the same article, the ZAKA volunteer team is today trained for such events.
According to the organization's website, the Defense Ministry recognizes ZAKA as an ‘aid organization in times of emergency’, and it trains with the Home Front Command.

Yechezkel Farkash, operations commander in the north, told of an apartment where the body of an 80-year-old woman, single and without children, was found, having remained there for several days after her death.
He said that when the cleaning was finished, the neighbors and the police applauded the team.
According to ynet, in recent years the volunteers have encountered many elderly people found dead in their apartments days after their death.
According to Farkash, singing together frees the heart from the hardships and helps the volunteers cope with difficult events.

Meshi-Zahav told eJewishPhilanthropy that he learned that what the organization does is in fact honoring the living, because the family needs to know that their loved one will receive a proper burial.
According to the Jerusalem Post, in 2019 ZAKA had 3,500 volunteers, mostly ultra-Orthodox, who help ambulance crews identify victims and gather remains and blood for burial.

According to an earlier article in the Forward, from the time of the interfaith declaration signed on January 4 in Zichron Yaakov (during the tenure of Chief Rabbi Yona Metzger), ZAKA then had 350 volunteers from religious minorities, alongside 1,150 Haredi volunteers and 350 non-Haredi Jews.
A volunteer from Kafr Qasim told the Forward that when he first volunteered with Haredim some people thought it was strange, but now it is totally accepted.

According to the Forward, ZAKA assembled some two dozen religious leaders, among them the Chief Rabbi, the head of the Druze community and the head of an association of imams, to sign a joint humanitarian declaration.
According to the Forward, Meshi-Zahav said that dialogue without actual action has no future.
According to the same newspaper, in one of the new initiatives Haredi and Muslim volunteers began running a course in accident prevention and first aid for women in Arab towns.
According to ynet, ZAKA set up a new unit, "The Volunteers among the People", in which every citizen will be able to volunteer for the first time, regardless of religion, race or sex.
The unit's volunteers will undergo one evening of training and keep in touch through a district WhatsApp group.

stations.title: The international unit goes out into the world

paragraphs.text: According to the organization's chairman, ZAKA's International Rescue Unit is recognized by the UN and goes to the ends of the earth.
The director of the International Division, Baruch Nidam, said that the division operates wherever disaster strikes.
ZAKA's director general, Dubi Weissenstern, said that ZAKA sees a moral duty to step forward and help other nations as well in disasters.
According to Weisenstern, ZAKA's international force is multicultural and trained to handle the dead in accordance with their religion and faith.
According to him, at least two people who speak the language of the country are sent on every international mission.
After the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami, ZAKA combed Thailand in search of 30 Israelis, out of nearly 300,000 dead, according to the article.
When a Germanwings plane crashed in the Alps, ZAKA personnel climbed the mountains to find the body of Eyal Baum, 39, from Hod HaSharon.
Two ZAKA delegations, from Israel and from Hong Kong, were set to leave for Japan after the end of Shabbat.
According to the article, during an earthquake in Japan a ZAKA team searched for bodies and assisted the injured alongside an Iranian team.
According to the article, ZAKA volunteers arrived within two hours at the scene of the shooting at the Tree of Life synagogue in Pittsburgh, where 11 people were shot dead.
According to the same source, after the attack on the Chabad House in Mumbai the volunteers realized they needed to set up teams around the world, available faster than the Israeli team.

According to JTA, the international unit assisted in the 2011 tsunami and earthquake in Japan, Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines in 2013, and the Nepal earthquake and the Paris terror attacks in 2015.

According to the Jerusalem Post, the Ethiopian authorities initially prevented the volunteers from reaching the scene, and only after the intervention of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu did they manage to reach it.

According to the same newspaper, in June 2019 the volunteers found the remains of Shimon Reem, and in September the identification of the remains of Avraham Matzliah was confirmed; both were Israelis killed in the crash.
The writer of an opinion piece in the newspaper wrote that it is hard to exaggerate the comfort families derive from the burial and from having a grave to visit.

stations.title: Nepal: two and a half weeks of searching

paragraphs.text: A joint mission of United Hatzalah and ZAKA was scheduled to leave Israel for Nepal on Sunday afternoon.
The delegation was prepared to assist with setting up field hospitals, handling bodies and rescuing those who were trapped.
According to the article, another unit of the emergency response organizations United Hatzalah, ZAKA and First Israel set out for more remote areas of Nepal.
ZAKA volunteer Yossi Frankel said that the mission includes returning the bodies of Jewish and Israeli tourists, and that the team is expected to stay there for at least two weeks.
ZAKA sent a team to find the Israeli backpacker Or Asraf, who was killed in the 2015 earthquake.
After a dam collapsed near Brumadinho, a delegation of ZAKA search and rescue workers and members of the Home Front Command left for Brazil.
ZAKA brought advanced equipment to the mission, including a recently purchased sonar device.
At the request of the Turkish authorities, an Israeli delegation of about 150 soldiers and officers from the Home Front Command set out, which also included ZAKA volunteers.
According to the report, the death toll from the earthquake then stood at more than 1,500 people.
Haim Weingarten of ZAKA said that the volunteers came to locate missing people, recover bodies and help the injured.
In Colombia, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the coastal province of Chocó.
The earthquake killed at least 250 people, and a delegation from ZAKA's International Division assisted in cities in Colombia.
The delegation included search and rescue personnel, doctors, engineers and experts in preserving the dignity of the dead, and they reached Cali, Pereira and Chocó.
ZAKA set up a temporary clinic at one of the destruction sites to provide immediate medical care.
Yosef Garmon said that they are operating for the Jewish community, but also for all residents.
Prime Minister Netanyahu said that another humanitarian delegation from Israel was expected to leave for Colombia in the coming days.

stations.title: Venezuela: no relations, but helping hands

paragraphs.text: Israel and Venezuela have had no diplomatic relations since Caracas severed them in 2009, following the conflict in Gaza.
According to Garmon, the airports in the region were closed, and the team entered overland through Colombia on a journey of more than 15 hours, before receiving authorization to operate.
The Israeli delegation included engineers, rescue specialists, paramedics, first responders and logistics personnel.
The head of the delegation, Nachman Dickstein, said that the work began immediately and continued for many hours at two disaster sites.
They worked inside collapsed and unstable buildings, and the work required risk assessments and close coordination.
ZAKA teams joined local emergency responders in Venezuela in searching collapsed buildings, recovering victims from the rubble and distributing food, medicine and medical supplies.
The organization also brought specialist physicians to relieve overloaded hospitals.
ZAKA worked with the International Humanitarian Coalition on search, medical assistance and humanitarian aid.
As part of the next phase of the Israeli aid operation in Venezuela, about 20 specialists assisted remotely from Israel in analyzing field data and preparing a long-term reconstruction strategy.
The Venezuelan authorities asked the Israeli delegation for additional assistance, even though there are no diplomatic relations.
According to Garmon, even institutions that had previously supported the Palestinian cause embraced the effort after working alongside the Israeli volunteers.
The organization is evaluating land for a new residential neighborhood for families who lost their homes, as in reconstruction projects it carried out in Guatemala.
Venezuela is home to a small Jewish community, estimated at between 3,000 and 5,000 people.
Among other awards, Meshi-Zahav received the Yigal Alon Prize in 2005, for outstanding pioneering service to Israeli society.

In a letter on the organization's website, ZAKA founder and chairman Yehuda Meshi Zahav wrote that ZAKA is ranked among Israelis as the second most esteemed organization after the IDF, without citing a source for the ranking.
According to Haim Weingarten, ZAKA volunteers represent the State of Israel and the values of compassion, dignity and professionalism.
According to JNS, since the October 7, 2023 massacre, 800 ZAKA volunteers have worked around the clock to recover the remains of the dead.
According to Ynetnews, around 200 volunteers worked at the Shura base in Ramla, to which approximately 1,200 bodies were transferred for identification in the days after the massacre.
Volunteer Eli Turgeman told Ynetnews that ZAKA volunteers were the first to open the body bags and see the devastation.
He said that a rabbinical ruling allowed them to continue working on weekends as well and to violate Shabbat, and that this was hard for him as a Haredi Jew.

Veteran volunteer Simcha Greiniman told JNS that after dealing with blown-up buses, restaurants and hotels and synagogues where massacres had taken place, there is no way to prepare for the sight of hundreds of bodies at a party in a field.

According to JNS, ZAKA generally refrains from photographing the deceased out of respect for their privacy, but after two days in the field Greiniman was instructed by his commanders to take pictures as evidence.
Meshi-Zahav resigned from the leadership of ZAKA and gave up the Israel Prize.
After October 7, ZAKA volunteers gave several false reports of Hamas atrocities, and the reports spread in the media.

According to Ynetnews, more than ten volunteers involved in the task reported that the packing of IDF casualty bags was done carelessly, bags were replaced without preserving identifying details, and important evidence was left in the field.
According to representatives of the military rabbinate, the replacement of the bags damaged the scant forensic evidence that had been collected.
ZAKA told Ynetnews that it was not possible to collect investigative findings in real time.

According to The Intercept, a Haaretz report found that after October 7 senior commanders sidelined IDF soldiers specializing in recovering bodies and preserving evidence, and brought in untrained ZAKA volunteers instead.
According to The Intercept, citing Haaretz, ZAKA did not document remains, put parts from different bodies in the same bag, and did not collect all the remains from the homes and the field.
According to The Intercept, sources from other rescue organizations saw ZAKA volunteers making fundraising calls and videos with bodies in the background.
According to The Intercept, Haaretz calculated that ZAKA has raised at least $13.7 million since the attacks.
According to The Intercept, Haaretz debunked Yossi Landau's story of a pregnant woman in Be'eri whose fetus had been cut out of her womb.
In a statement to Haaretz, ZAKA said that its volunteers are not pathology experts and do not have the professional tools to determine age or manner of murder, except for eyewitness testimony.

According to The Intercept, a volunteer adviser in the National Public Diplomacy Directorate at the Prime Minister's Office said that the testimonies of ZAKA volunteers had a decisive impact on exposing the atrocities to foreign journalists.
According to The Intercept, a 2022 Haaretz investigation found that ZAKA received millions of dollars in public funds while reporting more than three times the number of volunteers it had.
According to The Intercept, in the 1980s Meshi-Zahav led an extremist ultra-Orthodox movement called Keshet, which opposed archaeological digs and autopsies as religious desecration.
According to the same report, in 2021 more than a dozen people claimed that Meshi-Zahav had raped, assaulted and threatened them.
According to The Intercept, in 2014 the police closed the case against him without an indictment, even though it allegedly knew of at least 20 cases of sexual assault of minors.
According to The Intercept, shortly after the allegations were published Meshi-Zahav attempted suicide, and he died a year later.

disagreements.question: How many volunteers does ZAKA have?

versions.says: The organization's chairman: more than 3,000 volunteers in Israel
The eJewishPhilanthropy article: more than 3,500 volunteers in Israel
The organization itself claims: over 4,000 volunteers.

disagreements.question: How many people were killed in the earthquakes in Venezuela?

versions.says: Official Venezuelan figures, according to JNS: 3,535 dead, 16,470 injured and more than 17,000 homeless
i24NEWS headline, after 7 days: almost 2,000 confirmed dead and tens of thousands missing

claims.text: לפי JNS, זק"א נמנעת בדרך כלל מצילום הנפטרים מתוך כבוד לפרטיותם, אך גרינימן קיבל מהמפקדים הוראה לצלם כראיה לאחר יומיים בשטח.
claims.quote: While ZAKA generally refrains from photographing the deceased out of respect for their privacy, Greiniman was told by his commanders after two days in the field to take pictures as evidence of the horror.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, מתנדבי זק"א נמצאים לרוב בזירות פיגועים ותאונות דרכים קטלניות ואוספים שרידי גוף ודם לקבורה יהודית לפי ההלכה.
claims.quote: ZAKA volunteers are often on the scene of terror attacks and deadly road accidents, collecting body parts and blood for Jewish burials according to Jewish law.

claims.text: לפי JTA (2016), היחידה הבינלאומית של זק"א סייעה ברעידת האדמה בנפאל ובפיגועי פריז ב-2015, בטייפון הייאן בפיליפינים ב-2013 ובצונאמי ורעידת האדמה ביפן ב-2011.
claims.quote: Its international rescue unit has assisted in the Nepal earthquake and Paris terror attacks, both last year; Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines in 2013; the tsunami and earthquake in Japan in 2011

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-eJewishPhilanthropy, משי-זהב הבין שבאסון המשטרה חוסמת את הזירה ומאפשרת גישה רק לגורמים "רשמיים", ולכן הצוות שלו עבר מקצוענות.
claims.quote: quickly realized that when a disaster strikes, police barricade the scene and only allow “official” people access.

claims.text: ב-2019, לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, היו בזק"א 3,500 מתנדבים, רובם חרדים, שעוזרים לצוותי האמבולנס לזהות קורבנות ואוספים שרידים ודם לקבורה.
claims.quote: ZAKA today has 3,500 volunteers, mostly ultra-Orthodox, who help ambulance crews identify victims of terrorism and road accidents, and where needed, gather body parts and spilled blood for proper burial.

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט, משי-זהב ניסה להתאבד זמן קצר אחרי פרסום טענות ההתעללות ומת כעבור שנה.
claims.quote: Meshi-Zahav attempted suicide shortly after the abuse allegations were reported and died a year later.

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט, הארץ חישב שזק"א גייסה לפחות 13.7 מיליון דולר מאז הפיגועים.
claims.quote: Haaretz calculated that Zaka has raked in at least $13.7 million since the attacks.

claims.text: המתנדב אלי תורג'מן סיפר ל-Ynetnews שמתנדבי זק"א היו הראשונים שפתחו את שקי הגופות וראו את ההרס.
claims.quote: We were the first to open the body bags and witness the devastation.

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, מתנדבי זק"א תמיד האחרונים לעזוב זירת אירוע קטלני, אחרי שניקו את הדם ושרידי הגוף.
claims.quote: That is why our volunteers are always the last to leave the scene of a fatal incident, as they clear the area of spilled blood and human remains.

claims.text: מפקד מבצעים בצפון, יחזקאל פרקש, סיפר שבאחת הפעמים נמצאה דירה בה גופת אישה בת 80 רווקה וללא ילדים שנפטרה ונשארה ימים רבים.
claims.quote: An 80-year-old woman who lived in the apartment, single, without children, was found on the floor of her apartment, lying on the floor in the entry, dead.

claims.text: לפי eJewishPhilanthropy, ב-2001, בקריסת אולם ורסאי בירושלים באמצע חתונה, נפלו אל מותם 23 בני אדם ו-380 נפצעו; צוות מתנדבי זק"א מאומן כיום לאירועים כאלה.
claims.quote: Then, in 2001, when the third floor of the four-story Versailles wedding hall in Talpiot, Jerusalem collapsed during the wedding of Keren and Asaf Dror, 23 people fell to their deaths and another 380 people were injured.

claims.text: לפי אתר הארגון, משי-זהב היה במשך שלושים שנה חבר בעדה החרדית במאה שערים והשתתף בהפגנות נגד הממסד הציוני.
claims.quote: For thirty years, as a member of the Eda Haredit sect in Mea Shearim, Meshi-Zahav participated in demonstrations against the Zionist establishment

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט בציטוט הארץ, זק"א לא תיעדה שרידים, הניחה חלקים מגופות שונות באותו שק ולא אספה את כל השרידים מהבתים ומהשטח.
claims.quote: According to Haaretz, Zaka failed to document remains, put parts from different bodies in the same bag, and did not collect all the remains in homes and the field.

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט, הארץ הפריך את סיפורו של יוסי לנדאו על אישה בהיריון בבארי שעוברה הוצא מבטנה.
claims.quote: Haaretz debunked Landau’s tale of the pregnant woman’s corpse in Kibbutz Be’eri whose fetus was cut out by Hamas attackers.

claims.text: בפיגוע באוטובוס 405 נהרגו 16 בני אדם, ביניהם שני קנדים ואמריקאי, ו-27 נפצעו.
claims.quote: Sixteen people were killed, including two Canadians and an American, and 27 were injured.

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט, יועץ מתנדב במערך ההסברה הלאומי בלשכת ראש הממשלה אמר שעדויות מתנדבי זק"א השפיעו באופן מכריע על חשיפת הזוועות לעיתונאים זרים.
claims.quote: The testimonies of Zaka volunteers, as first responders on the ground, had a decisive impact in exposing the atrocities in the South to the foreign journalists covering the war

claims.text: לפי הפורוורד, בזק"א היו 350 מתנדבים ממיעוטים דתיים לצד 1,150 מתנדבים חרדים ו-350 יהודים לא חרדים.
claims.quote: ZAKA already has 350 volunteers from Israel’s minority religions, who serve alongside the organization’s 1,150 Haredi volunteers and 350 non-Haredi Jews.

claims.text: פרקש סיפר שבתום הניקיון בדירה השכנים והמשטרה מחאו לצוות כפיים על המשימה שביצע.
claims.quote: we went down to the street level, where we saw the police and the neighbors who gave us a round of applause for the holy task we had undertaken.

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט, מקורות מארגוני הצלה אחרים ראו מתנדבי זק"א מבצעים שיחות וסרטוני גיוס כספים כשגופות ברקע.
claims.quote: sources from other rescue groups observed Zaka volunteers make fundraising calls and videos with corpses in the background.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בתחילה מנעו הרשויות באתיופיה ממתנדבי זק"א להגיע לזירת ההתרסקות.
claims.quote: Initially, Ethiopian authorities prevented ZAKA workers from visiting the crash scene.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, לאחר התערבות ראש הממשלה בנימין נתניהו הצליחה זק"א להגיע לזירה באתיופיה.
claims.quote: After the intervention of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, ZAKA finally succeeded.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, ההלכה היהודית דורשת כבוד מרבי למת, כולל קבורה מהירה וקבורה של כל חלק בגוף.
claims.quote: Jewish law (Halacha) demands utmost respect for the dead, including a prompt burial, and burial of every part of the body.

claims.text: לפי תגובת זק"א ל-Ynetnews, לא ניתן היה לאסוף ממצאים חקירתיים בזמן אמת, והמרחבים נארזו בשקי זק"א או צה"ל כשלא הוחלף אף שק.
claims.quote: It was not feasible to collect investigative findings in real time, and the spaces were packed in ZAKA or IDF bags, no bags were changed.

claims.text: לפי האינטרספט, דו"ח של הארץ מצא שאחרי 7 באוקטובר מפקדים בכירים הרחיקו חיילי צה"ל המתמחים באיסוף גופות ושימור ראיות והביאו במקומם מתנדבי זק"א בלתי מיומנים.
claims.quote: A blockbuster Haaretz report found after October 7, senior military leaders sidelined Israel Defense Forces soldiers specializing in recovering bodies and preserving evidence and sent in untrained Zaka volunteers instead.

quote_translations.c61: At the request of the authorities in Turkey, an Israeli aid delegation numbering about 150 soldiers and officers in regular and reserve service from the Home Front Command will take off this evening (Monday)
quote_translations.c62: So far, the death toll in the severe disaster in Turkey itself stands at more than 1,500 people
quote_translations.c63: with the aim of assisting in locating the missing, recovering the bodies of the dead and providing assistance to the injured
quote_translations.c74: with other yeshiva students to give first aid to the injured
quote_translations.cm108: To join the unit, the volunteers will undergo one evening of training and admission to the unit and will keep in touch with a district WhatsApp group.
quote_translations.cm89: To save those who can be saved and to honor those who can now only be honored
quote_translations.cm107: The ZAKA organization (Disaster Victim Identification) decided to expand its ranks, and for the first time every citizen, man or woman, regardless of religion, race and sex, will be given the opportunity to volunteer in the organization
quote_translations.cm83: When the work of evacuating the many wounded from the scene, near the community of Telz Stone, was over, dozens of volunteers went down into the wadi and began to attend to the dead, the bloodstains and the remains that require burial.
quote_translations.cm97: In recent years ZAKA volunteers have encountered many elderly people who are found dead in their apartments days after they passed away.
